title: report.json - a council run, structured
description: The machine-readable record of one finished council run: runs/<id>/report.json, built by reportJsonShape() in src/report-shape.js for every writer (a normal run, a resumed run, `council init`/`council demo`, --rematch, --replay). BOARD.md is the same record for people; nothing should parse BOARD.md. A run that stopped early (spend cap, pre-flight block, external pause, crash) writes no report.json at all - its absence means 'not finished'. A run the per-run spend cap stopped (since 0.7.7), and since 0.8.1 an advice call stopped by a person, its client or its wall clock (exit 18), writes runs/<id>/report-partial.json instead: this same schema, built by the same function from what the run had when it stopped, plus `partial: true`, `stoppedBy` and `stoppedAtStage`. In it a stage the run never reached has the value that means 'did not run' (null, [], false, or the field absent); `passed`, `outcome` and `signoff` describe the state at the stop, not a verdict; `finished_at` is when the run stopped. A resume removes it together with STOPPED-budget.json; a resumed run that finishes writes report.json. Versioning: `schemaVersion` is an integer that moves only on a breaking change (a field renamed, removed, or its meaning or type changed). Adding a field is not breaking and does not move it, so a reader MUST ignore fields it does not know; that is why additionalProperties is left open everywhere. Each top-level property carries an `x-stability` annotation: `stable` fields keep their name, type and meaning for the whole of schemaVersion 1; `experimental` fields may change shape in a minor release and are listed in the changelog when they do. Fields marked 'model-supplied' come from a model's own JSON reply and are passed through with little or no checking: read them defensively.

schemaVersion.description: Format version of this file. Integer; bumped only on a breaking change. Absent on report.json files written before 0.7.7: read those as version 1.

name.description: The npm package that wrote the file: the-high-council.

version.description: Its version, from its package.json ('unknown' if unreadable).

producer.description: Which program, at which version, wrote this report. Added in 0.7.7; absent on earlier reports.

started_at.description: When the run's first sitting began (ISO 8601, UTC). For --rematch, --replay and init: when that run began. Absent on reports written before 0.7.7, and on a resumed run whose first sitting predates 0.7.7 (its run.json never recorded the time).

finished_at.description: When this report was written (ISO 8601, UTC): the end of the run's last sitting. Added in 0.7.7; absent on earlier reports. Time spent paused at an external seat falls between the two timestamps.

runId.description: The run folder's name: an ISO-8601 timestamp with ':' and '.' replaced by '-' (e.g. 2026-09-25T15-08-53-698Z), plus a suffix for derived runs ('-init', '.rematch-<n>', '.replay-<date>').

chain.description: The chain config's `name` (chains/<name>.json). Names the recipe, not its contents: the chain file can change after the run.

task.description: Path to the task file, never absolute: relative to the directory the run was started in (forward slashes), or the file name alone when the file lies outside it. Written the same way by every writer since 0.7.7; earlier reports carry an absolute path after --resume, --rematch, --replay and init. Still names a file on the author's disk: consider dropping it before publishing a run.

task_sha256.description: SHA-256 (hex) of the task file's UTF-8 text as the report's last sitting read it. Its first 12 characters are run.json's `taskHash`, the frozen-scope check a resume makes. Lets a reader match a report to a task file without the path. On an advice run the task file is the brief, so this is the hash of the exact text every seat was sent (the text the person confirmed). Added in 0.7.7; absent on earlier reports.

fromRun.description: The earlier run folder whose criteria (and first draft) this run reused via --from-run; null when the run wrote its own. Never absolute since 0.7.7: relative to the directory the run was started in (forward slashes), or the run folder's name alone when it lies outside it. Earlier reports can carry an absolute path, notably after --resume.

criteria.description: Acceptance criteria, written before any draft or debate, in the order the panel was asked to check them. Model-supplied: the criteria stage checks that the list is non-empty and not meta, not that each item is a string.

questions.description: Clarifying questions the planner asked before writing criteria, each with its own default. null when the chain has no questions stage (and on a descending-mode run). Absent on descending-mode reports written before 0.7.7.

passed.description: True if the panel signed off on the final draft under the chain's sign-off rule (`first`: one critic; `unanimous`: every critic on the same draft). Read `outcome` before quoting this: a run can pass with part of its roster unheard. On a report that carries `advise` (an advice call, not a plan) this is not a sign-off: nobody reviewed a draft, it is true whenever the call ran, and verdict_stats and metrics skip such reports.

outcome.description: Verdict class, computed by src/outcome.js from the rest of this file. `degraded` wins: a seated lab produced nothing usable (it dropped out, see `dropouts[]`: in a tiered chain this may be a debating seat that never votes), a reviewer abstained, no reviewer was heard, or the round fell short of the quorum - so the run did not have the roster the chain intended. Otherwise `consensus` if passed, else `no_consensus`. On a report that carries `advise` this is not a sign-off either: it says whether the advisors' answers agreed (see `advise`), and verdict_stats and metrics skip such reports.

lastCritique.description: The last review round's verdict. Unanimous chains: the union of every critic's failures, each tagged with `lab`. First-to-pass chains: the one critic's own parsed reply. null only if no review round ran.

signoff.description: One entry per critic seat ASKED in the final unanimous round (all of them on a flat panel). On a layered run (see `layers`) a seat whose layer was not asked in that round has no entry here: read `layers` for the layers that were never asked, and never infer a pass from this array alone. null on chains whose sign-off is `first` (see panelVerdicts for those).

proposals.description: Every proposal kept for the debate, one node per proposal. Empty when the chain has no proposal stage. A lab that produced none is not here: see dropouts.

dropouts.description: Seats that were on the roster but produced nothing usable (unreadable proposals after a retry, a provider failure in review). Count labs from here plus proposals, never from proposals alone.

roster_answers.description: Present only when the run had a session-seat stage (provider external). Who answered those stages, AS DECLARED by the MCP client and the session, never verified, and the review panel's company count as recorded beside the count the chain was designed for. A seat answered by a different model is not a dropout and does not change outcome. Added 0.8.3.

design_companies.description: Companies on the review panel by what the chain asks for.

recorded_companies.description: Companies on the review panel by what was recorded: model-API seats by their model, session seats by the model their answer declared.

unverified_seats.description: Session seats on the panel whose answer declared no model, or one this version has no company for.

company.description: The company of the declared model, or null when none was declared or this version has no row for it.

panel.description: True for a stage of the review panel (a judge): only these count in the company tally. Writer stages (build, revise, handoff) are listed but counted nowhere.

status.description: no-model-asked: the seat asks for no particular model (claude-code-session); never 'different' and never 'not-declared'.

debate.description: The anonymised argument over the proposals: posts (who said what about which proposal) and replies (what each author then did). null when the chain has no debate stage.

scoreboard.description: What the final plan did with each proposal, read from the plan's own 'Scope ledger' lines, per proposal and per lab. null when there were no proposals (and on a descending-mode run). Absent on descending-mode reports written before 0.7.7.

totals.description: Token and cost totals over every stage in `stages`, plus any superseded stages paid for earlier.

superseded.description: Optional. Present only when stages were set aside and paid for again: the superseded records `totals.supersededUsd` absorbed when this report was written, one { label, usd, reservationId } each (label is the file under superseded/; reservationId is null for a record written before 0.8.3), so the share of the total stays attributable if a file is later lost. Added in 0.8.3.

kind.description: Present on a charge record: waste (a discarded attempt) or billed (a call that was sent and may have been billed).

maxUsd.description: The per-run spend ceiling in USD this run was held to (--max-usd, MAX_USD_PER_RUN, or the default); null when the ceiling was disabled (--max-usd none) or, for init/rematch/replay, not recorded.

stages.description: One record per model call, in the order they were recorded (concurrent calls may interleave). The reply text itself is in <label>.md in the run folder, not here.

alternatives.description: Present only on chains with alternatives.enabled: one whole architecture per lab, written blind before the skeleton, and the same post/reply board the proposals get.

advise.description: Present only on advise chains (the council advisor): status, the headline leaning (field `verdict`: proceed, change, stop, need_information or split), agreement (unanimous, plurality or split) and tally, the text of the leaning (`verdict_text`), every seat's first (blind) and final position with quote-checked risks, the debate rounds and why the debate stopped, the dissent (every position that is not the headline, in the seat's own words), what the brief was missing, dropouts, the call's own ceiling and what it spent. Agreement is a process signal, not a finding that the advice is right, and it is vacuous for a single seat or for several samples of one model (`outcome` reads `consensus` for those; read `advise.seats_asked` and the tally). Seat-written fields are model-supplied. `advise.sent_to` and `advise.dispositions` (brief 29) say where the brief went and what the caller recorded before the call; the brief's own hash is the top-level `task_sha256`, because the brief is the run's task file (0.8.1 naming pass). For a report with `advise`, `passed` and `outcome` are not a sign-off (see both).

sent_to.description: One row per seat the brief went to (the panel, then the synthesis seat when there is one): lab, model, provider, the retention wording the send preview showed ("ZDR-tagged by OpenRouter" is OpenRouter's routing tag, not a guarantee; "retains, ..." quotes the lab's own page; "unknown"), its class, and the hosts the provider said answered (`served_by`, empty when none named one). Read from a dated table (src/advice-retention.json). Added after 0.7.9.

dispositions.description: On advice runs started by the MCP tools: the accept, reject or defer (with a reason) the caller recorded, before this call, for each objection of the previous advice call (`id` is `<run>#<lab>`). Empty when there was nothing to record. Model-supplied text. Added after 0.7.9.

deep_dive.description: Present only on chains with deep_dive.enabled (tiered councils): the one deep-dive seat's calls, its own dollar cap, what it spent, why it stopped (null, own_cap or max_calls) and its findings, each with a quote_status. The findings are not votes; under "judging": "all-roles" the same lab may also judge on the panel.

decision.description: Model-supplied: the decision the challenger re-opened.

evidence_needed.description: Model-supplied: what evidence would settle it.

reopened_rounds.description: Always 1 today: one challenge re-opens one decision for one round.

challenge.description: Post-sign-off challenge stage (challenge.enabled). null when the chain does not enable it.

engaged.description: False when the reviser left the draft byte-for-byte unchanged (a rubber stamp).

allocator.description: Extra rounds aimed at the most contested criterion (allocator.enabled). null when off.

round.description: A review round number, or one of the strings 'build' (the builder's own DECLINED lines, since 0.8.1), 'dispute', 'challenge', 'allocator-<n>' for text written outside the numbered rounds. Mixed type: see the report's fix list.

reason.description: Model-supplied: why the reviser declined this objection.

objection_id.description: The id of the objection this DECLINED line answered, when the reviser named one (a chain with answer_back.enabled whose prompt asks for it). Absent when it named none. Added in 0.8.2.

disputes.description: Objections the builder or the reviser declined and kept out of the deliverable (their DECLINED lines). Not the same thing as `dispute`.

orphanSections.description: Sections left with no surviving owner after a withdrawal chain cycled or dead-ended. [] on a descending-mode run; absent on descending-mode reports written before 0.7.7.

withdrawalCycles.description: How many withdrawal chains cycled (e.g. two labs withdrawing in each other's favour). 0 on a descending-mode run; absent on descending-mode reports written before 0.7.7.

lane.description: 0.8.2 (item 7): the review lane of this seat, present only when the seat has one (the optional plan-lanes-4 chain).

envelope.description: Present only on an unheard row of a run that used the verdict envelope (see `verdict_envelope`), and only when the reply was a complete JSON object that carried no review_id and draft_id for this call (`missing`) or ids that were not this call's (`wrong_id`). A reply that was cut off, ended by an error, ran out of reasoning or was not a JSON object at all keeps its `reason_code` and has no `envelope`: its absence never means the ids were fine. `reason_code` keeps its own value.

no_answer.description: Present only on an unheard seat whose reply was cut off at its cap after spending its tokens on thinking and carried no text: "no answer: thinking used the whole cap". The seat is unheard (an unreadable non-pass), never a pass. Added in 0.8.1.

table_gap.description: Present only on an unheard seat refused for an incomplete sign-off table (reason_code INCOMPLETE_TABLE, chains with signoff_table.required): what the table lacked. Added in 0.8.2.

reasked.description: True if a re-ask call was made for this seat this round. False otherwise, even when its first reply was not counted.

carried.description: Present and true when the seat was not asked this round: the draft was byte-identical to the last round's, where this seat was heard and clean, and only the unheard seat(s) were asked again (0.7.9). Absent otherwise.

layer.description: 0.8.3: the layer the seat sits in. Present only on a layered chain. A seat whose layer was not asked in a round has NO row here for that round; `layers` records it as not_asked.

from_round.description: 0.8.3: on a carried verdict of a layered chain, the round in which the verdict was given (no new call, no new charge).

panelVerdicts.description: Every critic's verdict in every review round, both sign-off modes. The per-round history that signoff[] (final round only) does not keep.

regressions.description: Criteria that had been met and then failed again in a later round, with the labs that failed them.

reason.description: early_finish (0.8.3, a closed enum widened: a reader that validates `reason` strictly must accept it): the run finished early at the session's proposal with the overseer layer's yes (see `stop`); no round cap was reached. layer_not_signed_off (0.8.3): a layered run stopped because a layer gave no usable verdict or the top layer did not sign off explicitly (see layerStop). finish_chosen (0.8.3): the person chose to finish after the run stopped at an overseer or layer limit (see `stop`).

not_asked_in_final_round.description: 0.8.3, layered chains: the lab raised this in last_raised_round and its layer was not asked in the final round, so it may already be fixed in the final draft.

review.description: Present when the chain sets dispute.review: per-objection checks of how the draft handled it.

dispute.description: Present only on chains with dispute.enabled: whether the dispute stage ran, why, and the objections left open (recorded at the top of the deliverable).

title.description: Model-supplied proposal title, or null if the id is unknown.

posts.description: The debate posts on this proposal, without `on` (it is the group's).

disagreement_groups.description: Present only when the run debated: the debate's posts grouped by the proposal they argue about. Derived from debate and proposals; adds no new facts.

result.description: The tool's own result: ok, exitCode, stdout, stderr and so on.

ground_truth.description: Present only on chains with verify.enabled: allowlisted tool results shown verbatim to later stages.

lints.description: Present only on chains with lints.enabled: deterministic plan lints. Informational, never a failure.

claims.description: Present only on chains with claims.enabled: objections restated with typed evidence. Claims whose evidence failed the offline check are dropped (and listed in WARNINGS.md).

warnings.description: 0.8.2, additive: a check that did not refuse the run but is worth knowing (max_usd_per_run: the expected cost fits the limit, the dry run's maximum is over it). Absent when there was none.

policy.description: Present only when a policy.json was in force: the checks it configured. Absent means no policy.

gate.description: Judged from the findings, never from the seat's own verdict. not_judged is never a pass.

security_review.description: Present only on chains with security_review.enabled: the final read-only security gate. Same object as security-review.json in the run folder.

on.description: Proposal id the canary objection was posted on.

capitulated.description: True if the author amended or withdrew in answer to an evidence-free objection.

no_quote_mark.description: Only in a chain with debate_hygiene.noQuoteMarks: true when the canary was shown to the author through the "[no quote]" mark like every other post that quotes nothing, false when the reply prompt in use did not render marks. Capitulation rates are not comparable across the two without saying so. Added in 0.8.2.

canary.description: Present only when a canary objection was sampled into the debate (canary.enabled). The canary post and reply are also in debate.posts/replies, each with canary: true and by: 'canary'.

quoteFindings.description: Present when the task fenced source text: one human-readable line per objection whose quote could not be found in that source, or that quoted nothing. Nothing is dropped because of these.

patchFallbacks.description: Present on chains with revise.mode 'patch': rounds where the reviser's patch could not be applied and a whole-draft revision was used instead.

status.description: 0.8.2: not_judged when the seat could not be reached or its reply could not be read; raised is then false but that is NOT 'no contradictions' - nobody did the check. Absent on a report written before 0.8.2 (read it as judged).

reason_code.description: 0.8.2: why the cold read is not_judged.

coldRead.description: Present only on chains with coldRead.enabled: a fresh seat that saw only the final draft (since 0.8.2, the text that is delivered, after any final edit), listing contradictions between its sections. Its findings, or the fact that it was not judged, are also written into the deliverable and WARNINGS.md.

layer.description: 0.8.3: on a layered chain, the layer in which nobody was heard.

noHeardReviewer.description: Present only when a review round heard no reviewer at all and the loop stopped there. Makes outcome 'degraded'.

overseer_round.description: 0.8.3, present only on a chain with overseer rounds (maxOverseerRounds): the overseer round this pass belongs to. A round ends only when the top layer gives a verdict; `round` stays the pass number and the stage labels never change.

state.description: signed_off: every seat of the layer was heard and clear. objected: a seat objected. unheard: nobody objected but a seat was not heard. abstained: asked, but no usable verdict (only stated passes, or in the top layer a seat that did not sign off explicitly). not_asked: a layer below did not sign off, so this one was not started. unfinished: asked and interrupted (a stop, a cap, a wall clock) before it finished.

ledger.description: Present only on a row of the TOP layer that was shown the objection ledger (a layered chain with answer_back): how many objection rows the section held (rows), how many were open (active), how many closed ones were left out (closed_cut), and the size of the section as sent (chars, and tokens_est = an estimate from UTF-8 bytes / 4 that under-counts non-Latin text). Counts only: the text is in the stage prompt, never copied here.

carried.description: Seats of this layer whose verdict is carried from an earlier round on the same unchanged draft (no new call, no new charge).

layers.description: 0.8.3, present only on a layered chain (seats.critics[].layer): one row per round per layer, in layer order. A layer that was not asked in a round is a row with state not_asked, never an absent row. signoff[] and panelVerdicts[] list asked seats only; this is where the layers that were not asked are recorded.

review_notes.description: 0.8.3 notes lane, present only when the chain's reviewNotes switch was on and the lane ran. Each judge's capped proposals and improvement ideas, as the judge wrote them (quoted model text; they decide nothing in the plan): the items kept within the per-round cap with who raised the same exact text in the same overseer round (raised_by), what was cut for the per-round cap (cut), the replies whose notes were not read and why (dropped), and how many items were longer than the length the judge was asked to keep (long). Each item's attempt names the stage file that holds the reply it came from: an empty string for the judge's first reply of the pass, otherwise the suffix of that file's label (for example reask1, reask2, answered, retry). A seat's items from every reply of a pass are read when the seat ends the pass with a verdict; counted in dropped instead are the replies of a seat that ends it unheard (verdict_not_recorded), replies a provider cut off or ended early (reply_cut_off, reply_incomplete) and an id the judge already gave in an earlier reply of the same pass (duplicate_of_earlier_reply). Each item's answer is what the writer replied, recorded as it was given (status taken, declined, same, unanswered, conflicting or builder_task) and the stage that carried it (from); the writer's claim is not checked. answers_from lists the stages that carried answers, as stage labels (revise-N, revise-N-full, handoff, notes-answer); answer.ending, on an answer given after the panel ended (handoff, notes-answer), names how the panel ended (signed_off, finish_chosen, layer_stop, no_reviewer_heard, not_quorate, not_signed_off); answer_counts counts what the writer wrote that did not become an answer (a line naming no item, a SAME with no valid target, malformed, repeated or reasonless lines, and a later different answer for an id already answered).

pass.description: The review pass in which the conflict was found.

label.description: The decider stage's label (conflict-<pass>), absent when no call was made.

kind.description: external: the decider is the person's session (the run pauses for its answer); seat: a paid seat; none: the chain names no decider.

shares_lab_with.description: The labs of the conflict that the decider's own lab equals: a ruling by one of the two sides is visible.

ids.description: The objection that came back first, then the objections fixed in between.

overseer_round.description: Present only on a chain with overseer rounds: the overseer round this pass belongs to.

rounds.description: Parallel to ids: the pass each objection was raised in.

silent_round.description: The pass in which the first objection's judge was asked and did not list it (the evidence for the swing).

prevail.description: An id from ids, or "neither". A ruling annotates; it never closes an objection.

why.description: Present when decided is false: why nobody ruled; person_asked: the decider asked for the person and the run stopped for the answer. Present with decided true on tree_member: the ask is not offered to a tree member, so the applied side is neither.

via.description: Present when the person chose (the channel: cli); no actor is claimed.

decider_prevail.description: What the decider leaned to when it asked for the person (or when the applied side is not its own).

decisions.description: 0.8.3 E4b, additive, present only when the layered panel found a conflict (an objection from a judge of one layer came back after the writer revised the plan in response to an objection from another layer): one row per conflict, with the ruling or the reason nobody ruled.

overseer_rounds.description: 0.8.3, present only on a chain with overseer rounds: how many overseer rounds are complete (the top layer gave a verdict in each).

kind.description: overseer_cap and layer_bound: a limit the run stopped at. early_finish (added in 0.8.3, a closed enum widened: a reader that validates kind strictly must accept it): the run FINISHED early at the session's proposal with the overseer layer's yes; it is NOT agreement (passed false, outcome not widened, exit 22).

why.description: layer_bound only: the layer used all the revisions it is allowed in one overseer round, or a seat of it stayed silent for too many passes in a row.

reason.description: early_finish only. MODEL-SUPPLIED: the session's own written reason, as it wrote it (cut at 1000 characters). A claim, not a finding.

declined_reason.description: Present only when handled is declined: the reason the reviser gave for declining this objection, as it wrote it (cut at 600 characters). MODEL-SUPPLIED: a claim, not a finding.

items.description: early_finish only. Every objection of the pass that triggered the revise, derived from the record (never from the session's words), with what the revise did: declined with a reason, changed, unchanged, or open (the chain records no objection ids). They are handed to the builder.

overseer.description: early_finish only: the labs of the overseer layer that said yes.

chosen.description: `early` (kind early_finish only): the run ended at the session's proposal and the overseer layer's yes, nobody chose it at a limit. `finish`: Present only when the person ended the stopped run with --finish: the run then finished as not agreed and the stop is kept in report.json with this field. A stop that is still waiting for the person's choice has no `chosen`.

stop.description: 0.8.3. Two shapes, both NOT agreement. (1) kind overseer_cap or layer_bound: present in report-partial.json of a layered run that stopped at the overseer-round cap or at a layer's bound (`why` says which: the layer used all the revisions it is allowed in one overseer round, or a seat of it stayed silent for too many passes in a row); the run is resumable and the person chooses to continue or to finish; present in report.json of such a run once the person finished it with --finish (then with `chosen: finish`). (2) kind early_finish: report.json ONLY (never report-partial; the run is not resumable, it finished) of a layered run whose session reviser proposed to finish early and whose overseer layer said yes (`chosen: early`); passed is false and exit 22 follows. Never in report.json of a run that neither stopped nor finished early.

ledger.description: With reason ledger_overflow: the size of the objection ledger that did not fit (the open objections alone exceeded the budget), so nothing was sent to the top layer.

layerStop.description: 0.8.3, present only when a layered run stopped because a layer ended it with no objection and no usable vote: nobody in the layer gave a verdict (only_stated_passes), a seat of the top layer stated a pass instead of signing off (top_layer_not_explicit; labs names them), or there was nothing to revise against (no_objection_to_revise). Not agreement: passed is false.

heard.description: Reviewers that gave a verdict (signed off or objected) that round.

passedOnly.description: Reviewers that only stated a pass.

notQuorate.description: Since 0.7.8. Present only when the chain sets quorum.minHeard and a review round in which every verdict was a sign-off had fewer verdicts than that; the loop stopped there. Not agreement: passed is false and outcome is 'degraded'.

unverifiedReplays.description: Present only when some stage was replayed from the stage cache but could be checked only against the task and chain, not the exact prompt.

argued.description: Present only on chains with argued.enabled: where the 'How this plan was argued' text is, and the check of every id and lab it names against this run's record.

criteria_sha256.description: sha256 over the criteria list, each criterion collapsed to one line, order counted (0.8.0). The same fingerprint the HANDOFF.md lock block carries; `council check-lock` compares them.

field_cuts.description: Every model-written field the harness cut before the next stages read it (0.8.1): a whole architecture's field, a debate post or reply longer than its seat's own token cap allowed (at least 40,000 characters), or a critic field over 8,000 characters. One row per cut, also written to WARNINGS.md. Absent when nothing was cut; absent on reports written before 0.8.1, which cut at 2,000 characters without a record.

stage.description: The stage whose reply held the field, when known.

checks_sha256.description: sha256 over how each criterion is checked, index-aligned with `criteria`: for a checkable criterion its `check` and `on` (from `criteria_kinds`), null for every other one, order counted (0.8.1). criteria_sha256 covers the wording only, so an edited check changes this and not that. The HANDOFF.md lock block carries the same hash in its second marker (`the-high-council:criteria-checks`); `council check-lock` compares them. Absent on reports written before 0.8.1.

criteria_lints.description: Word-level lints over the acceptance criteria, run before any paid review round (0.8.0). Heuristics: they miss a rephrasing and can flag a good criterion. Recorded only: never a stop. [] when clean.

signoff_table_gaps.description: Sign-offs refused because the per-criterion table was not full (a row for every criterion, each with evidence and a verdict that says MET or FAILED), on a chain with signoff_table.required. Present only when there was one. The seat counted as unheard (an abstention), never as consent. Added in 0.8.2.

outside_criteria_rows.description: Table rows a reply carried that named none of the criteria (ticket 16): recorded, never counted for or against any seat. Present only when there were some. Added in 0.8.2.

answer_back.description: With answer_back.enabled: for each judge that had objections in the previous round, the round it will see them in, their ids, how many DECLINED reasons the writer gave and how many passages of the draft changed. Summary only. Present only on such chains. Added in 0.8.2 (src/answer-back.js). On a layered chain a judge keeps its open objections until it is next asked, so a row is written in the round the judge is shown them (not the round after the revise) and `raised_round` names the round it first raised them (0.8.3).

signed_text.description: 0.8.2 (A3/F1): the draft last put to the panel: its sha256, the last panel round, whether the panel signed it (in a round where no seat could be heard the draft was shown but nobody read it). When it did not, label is 'not_accepted' and open_objections says how many objections were still open. Present on a finished run. `passed` is not touched by any of this.

delivered_text.description: 0.8.2 (A3/F1): the text delivered (deliverable.md). sha256 is of the whole file; body_sha256 of the model-written body without the harness's own blocks. same_as_signed is true when no model stage changed the body after the panel's last review (a harness note alone does not count). changed_by names the model stages that did (dispute, challenge, final_edit); harness_notes the blocks the harness wrote (dissent_block, cold_read_block). re_reviewed is false: the panel is not re-run on a changed text.

handoff_milestones.description: 0.8.2 (item 6c): present only when the chain sets handoff_contract.milestones. What the $0 lint found in the milestones the handoff seat wrote: the Status line (null when absent), how many milestones were parsed, and the findings (no_milestones, no_status, bad_status, duplicate_milestone, milestone_no_check, check_without_expected, unknown_criterion, criterion_not_discharged, discharge_not_checked, status_not_ready). A finding never changes passed.

split_contract.description: 0.8.3 (M3): present only when the plan holds a block marked the-high-council:tree-split. What the $0 block-local checks of the split contract found: the sha256 of the block as canonical JSON (null when it does not parse), whether every check passed, and the findings (the check number, a stable rule name and the words). It never changes `passed`; the tree applies the checks that need it (an ancestor's obligations and questions) again at expansion.

verdict_envelope.description: Present (true) only on a run that used the verdict envelope: each critic call carried a fresh review_id and draft_id, recorded in `<label>.envelope.json`, and a reply without them was not read as a verdict. Absent means the run did not use it.

tree.description: 0.8.3 (M6): present only on a member run of a recursive-councils tree: the member's lineage, copied unchanged from the `tree` field of its run.json. treeId is the run id of the tree's root run (the folder that holds `tree/`); node is the logical position, a path of milestone ids from the root (R, R/M2, ...); generation counts how often a decision has replaced that node (1 = the first); attempt counts starts of the same node and generation; parentNode and depth place it in the tree (null for the root); splitSha256 is the hash of the split block the node was derived from and bundleSha256 the hash of its input bundle (null where the tree has not computed them). A run that is no tree member has no `tree` key.

thin_contract.description: 0.8.2 (item 6a, the thin contract): one record of what this run was asked, graded against, shown and signed, all full-width sha256. task_sha256, criteria_sha256 and checks_sha256 repeat the fields of the same names; signed_text_sha256 is signed_text.sha256 (item 4). evidence.context_sha256 is the hash of the --context documents as the harness appended them (null when there were none); evidence.ground_truth_sha256 is the hash of the tool results the run recorded as shown (null when none), canonical JSON of each { tool, args, result } without result_ref. `sha256` is over the record without that field: canonical JSON, keys sorted at every depth, no whitespace, UTF-8, an unknown component the literal null. Tamper-evident, not tamper-proof: `council contract check <run>` recomputes what the folder still holds. Absent for an advice run and for a run with no criteria, task text or signed text.

handoff_text.description: 0.8.2 (F1): present when the chain has a handoff stage. made_from_sha256 is the text the handoff stage was given; made_from_signed is true only when that is exactly the text the panel signed; panel_reviewed is false (no panel reads a handoff). file_sha256 is the sha256 of HANDOFF.md as written, banner and lock block included; it is present only when this run wrote that file (a --rematch or --replay report has no file_sha256).

answer_back_replies.description: With answer_back.enabled: what each judge said about its own earlier objections (the `answers` array of its reply) and what the harness did with it: withdrawn (a quote from the draft was given), withdrawal_refused (no quote found in the draft: the objection stays open), sustained, unknown_id, unreadable_answer (a status that is neither sustained nor withdrawn: the objection stays open), unanswered (no answer at all: since the release after 0.8.2 the judge is asked once more when it signed off clean, and an objection still unanswered stays open, in signoff[].objections with carried_from_round). Present only when there were answers or own objections to answer. Added in 0.8.2. stated_pass_open (0.8.3, layered chains): the judge stated a pass while it still held this objection; a pass is not a withdrawal, so the objection stays open and that pass does not count as sign-off. quoted_from, quoted_ref, quoted_layer (0.8.3, layered chains with answer_back): on a withdrawn row, no quoted_from means the quote was found in the current draft; quoted_from "reviewer" means it was found in another judge's recorded row, named by quoted_ref (the lab) and quoted_layer (that row's layer), and the three appear together or not at all.

debate_orders.description: With debate_hygiene.shuffle: what each debate reader saw - the item ids (proposals, or alternatives) in the order it was shown them and the lab letter each lab had in its prompt. Present only on such chains. On such a chain the free text of debate.posts[] is re-lettered to real ids and lab names, so one lettering reads the whole record. Added in 0.8.2.

criteria_ids.description: Positional ids for `criteria`, index-aligned: C1, C2, ... (0.8.0).

missing_criteria.description: Sign-offs whose criteria table left criteria out (0.8.0). Recorded only: no verdict, prompt or stop reads it. [] when there were none. A reply with no table at all is not listed.

cut_despite_support.description: Proposals the plan cut although another lab supported them in the debate (0.8.0). Derived from proposals[] and debate.posts[]; present only when the run had both.

disagreement_map.description: One row per review round: each lab's verdict and the counts (0.8.0). Derived from panelVerdicts[]. A verdict marked `(carried)` was reused on an unchanged draft.

check.description: The command, test or measurement that settles it (model-supplied).

on.description: plan or build: what the check runs against.

downgraded.description: Why a criterion marked checkable was counted as judgement (it named no check).

criteria_kinds.description: Present only on chains with criteria_kinds.enabled. Index-aligned with `criteria`: whether a named check settles each criterion (checkable) or a reader's judgement does. kind is null when the seat classified nothing.

criteria_summary.description: Present only on chains with criteria_kinds.enabled: counts over criteria_kinds and criteria_met_without_evidence.

criteria_met_without_evidence.description: Present only on chains with criteria_kinds.enabled: every MET verdict on a checkable criterion that cited no evidence. Counted on the board; it does not overturn the verdict.

partial.description: Present, and true, only in report-partial.json: the run did not finish and this is what it had when it stopped. Never present in report.json. Added in 0.7.7.

stoppedBy.description: report-partial.json only: what stopped the run. `overseer_cap` and `layer_bound` (0.8.3): a layered run used all its allowed overseer rounds and the top layer still objected, or a layer needed more than its allowed revisions, or a seat of a layer stayed silent for too many passes in a row; it is resumable, NOT agreed, and exits 23 (the `stop` object says which). `budget` is the per-run spend cap (--max-usd; exit 4). Since 0.8.1 an advice call also writes a partial report when it is stopped (exit 18): `user` (a person, `council stop`), `client_cancel` (the MCP client cancelled the call or went away) or `wall_clock` (the chain's advise.max_wall_ms passed); its `advise` holds the answers that were paid for. A reader must ignore a value it does not know. Added in 0.7.7; values added in 0.8.1.

stoppedAtStage.description: report-partial.json only: the label of the stage the run stopped before (never called, never paid for) - the stage STOPPED-budget.json's `stoppedAt` names. Added in 0.7.7.

abstentionReason.description: Closed set (RESERVED_ABSTENTION_REASONS in src/chain.js): why a seat gave no usable reply.

default.description: Model-supplied: the answer the plan assumes if nobody answers.

criterion.description: The criterion text this objection is against (or a harness placeholder when the critic named none).

lab.description: Present in lastCritique.failures on unanimous chains: the lab that raised it.

id.description: 0.8.2, additive: a stable id for the problem, the same in every round the same lab raises the same criterion about the same quoted text (src/objection-ids.js).

criteria.description: Model-supplied per-criterion table, when the critic gave one.

dropped.description: True when the last critic failed at the provider and the round was recorded as a failure.

provider.description: Deprecated: use `lab`, which holds the same value. Despite the name, this is the seat's LAB (labOf(seat): `lab` if set, else the provider), not its transport provider. Kept for compatibility; removed only in schemaVersion 2.

lab.description: The seat's lab (labOf(seat): `lab` if set, else the provider), the independence accounting key. Added in 0.7.7; absent on earlier reports, where `provider` holds this value.

signedOff.description: true: signed off. false: objected (see objections). null: gave no verdict - abstained or stated a pass.

objections.description: Why the seat declined, on its own record. [] for a seat that signed off; null when signedOff is null.

passed.description: True if the seat stated a pass (declined to give a verdict, with a reason). Not the same as the top-level `passed`.

seat_index.description: The seat's index in the chain's seats.critics (0.7.9). A relay panel lists signoff[] in its review order, so array position is not the seat; replay and rematch diffs key on this. Absent on earlier reports.

layer.description: 0.8.3: the layer the seat sits in (seats.critics[].layer). Present only on a layered chain.

id.description: Harness-made: the lab tag in capitals, a counter if the tag repeats, '-', and the proposal's number (e.g. MOCKA-1). The model's own id, if it gave one, is kept as proposer_id.

lab.description: The proposing seat's lab (independence accounting key).

slice.description: The per-seat instruction slice that produced this proposal, if the chain partitions the work.

serves.description: Model-supplied: which criterion or goal it serves.

how.description: Model-supplied; replaced by the author's amendment when amended.

acceptance_test.description: Model-supplied; replaced by the author's amendment when amended.

amended.description: Present and true when the author amended it after the debate.

withdrawn.description: Present and true when the author withdrew it.

replaced_by.description: When withdrawn in favour of another proposal: that proposal's id (checked to exist).

proposer_id.description: The model's own id field, kept for the record.

proposer_lab.description: The model's own lab field, kept for the record.

by.description: Lab that posted, or 'canary' for an injected canary objection.

on.description: Id of the proposal (or alternative) the post is about; never the poster's own.

merge_with.description: With stance 'merge': the other id to merge with (checked to exist).

quoted.description: Only on an objection or merge post of a chain with debate_hygiene.noQuoteMarks: whether the post quotes (a quoted span of at least 8 characters) text that appears in the proposal it is about. false = 'no quote'. Added in 0.8.2 (src/post-quotes.js); detection only, no verdict reads it.

id.description: The author's own proposal (or alternative) id.

replaced_by.description: With action 'withdraw': the id it defers to (checked to exist).

how.description: Model-supplied; an amend usually brings the new how.

acceptance_test.description: Model-supplied; an amend may bring a new one.

reply.description: Built by spreading the model's own reply object and normalising id/action/replaced_by over it, so it may carry more model-supplied keys.

tie_break.description: Experimental. Always { occurred: false } today: no debate step decides by vote yet.

diagnostics.description: Experimental. Role failure-mode diagnostics computed from this run's own posts (src/role-diagnostics.js): perSeat, pairwiseAgreement, roleVsPlainSubstanceGap, flags.

dropped.description: Experimental (0.7.8). Debate posts and author replies the stage's filters rejected, one row per stage, lab and reason; [] when none were. Absent in runs made before 0.7.8. Reasons: for stage 'debate' unknown_target, own_proposal, bad_stance, unreadable, provider_error; for stage 'replies' unknown_target, not_own_proposal, not_posted_on, bad_action, unreadable, provider_error. An 'unreadable' row counts whole replies that did not parse, not posts; 'provider_error' (0.7.9) counts whole replies the provider ended with stop error, content_filter or refusal on the first try and on its one retry.

by.description: The lab whose post or reply was dropped.

status.description: From the plan's 'Scope ledger' line for this id; 'unaccounted' if the plan never mentions it.

built.description: Always null when written: left for a person to fill in after the build session.

reason_code.description: Why the seat produced nothing, in the same spelling as signoff[] and panelVerdicts[]. Written on alternatives dropouts since 0.7.7.

reasonCode.description: Deprecated alias of reason_code, same value; written on alternatives dropouts only. Removed only in schemaVersion 2.

cappedAt.description: Optional. The output cap this reply was asked at: the seat's own cap, or the bigger one an Anthropic seat was retried at after its thinking used the whole cap. Present on every stage that went through a call. Added in 0.8.1.

noAnswer.const: no answer: thinking used the whole cap
noAnswer.description: Optional. Present when the reply was cut off at its cap after spending its tokens on thinking and carried no text: the seat has no answer (an unreadable non-pass, never a pass). Added in 0.8.1.

reservationId.description: Optional. The id (r1, r2, ...) of the spend reservation written before the call that paid for this stage was sent (spend-reservations.jsonl), so a charge can be matched to its reservation even when a label was run twice. Absent when the stage wrote no reservation (a mock stage, or a call projected at $0). A cached replay carries the id of the sitting that paid. Added in 0.8.3.

label.description: Stable stage label; <label>.md in the run folder holds the reply text.

usd.description: What this call cost, including any attempt thrown away and retried.

priced.description: False when the model has no price in pricing.json: usd is then 0 and means 'unknown', not 'free'.

cached.description: True when replayed from <label>.md on disk at no cost.

asked_for.description: Session-seat stages only (provider external): the model the chain's seat asks for (for example subscription:opus-5.5), or claude-code-session when it asks for none. Added 0.8.3, additive.

answered_by.description: Session-seat stages only, when the answer arrived through submit_stage: who answered, AS DECLARED by the MCP client and by the session. Never verified: a client can say anything. Absent when the answer was written as a file by hand. Added 0.8.3, additive.

model.description: The model the session said wrote the answer, or null when it did not say.

declared_by.description: caller: a model was passed; client: only the client's name; none: neither.

usd.description: Priced spend only; includes supersededUsd when present.

unpriced.description: provider/model pairs with no price: their spend is not in usd.

supersededUsd.description: Present when stages were paid for and later superseded (a resume that re-ran them).
